q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: She went to the market yesterday.
explain: Past simple: subject + went + place + time.

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: We are going to bake a cake.
explain: 'be going to' + verb for plans.

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: Have you ever eaten candy floss?
explain: Present perfect question: Have + you + ever + past participle.

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: The bakery is bigger than the sweet shop.
explain: Comparative: bigger than.

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: I was walking home when it started to rain.
explain: Past continuous (was walking) interrupted by past simple (started).

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: You mustn't eat sweets before dinner.
explain: 'mustn't' = it is not allowed.

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: There isn't much sugar in the jar.
explain: 'much' with uncountable nouns like sugar.

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
explain: Present perfect + since + a point in time.

q: I ___ to the cinema last night.
explain: Last night is a finished past time, so use the past simple: go → went. Example: I went home.

notes.have gone: Have gone can't go with a finished time like 'last night'.

q: This cake is ___ than that one.
explain: Short adjectives add -er to compare: sweet → sweeter. Example: A cat is smaller than a dog.

notes.more sweet: More is for long adjectives: more beautiful. Sweet is short.
notes.sweetest: Sweetest compares three or more: the sweetest.
notes.sweet: With 'than' we need the comparative form.

q: How ___ apples do you need?
explain: How many is for things we can count. Example: How many eggs?

notes.much: How much is for things we can't count: How much milk?
notes.lot: Lot needs 'a lot of', and doesn't follow 'how'.

q: We ___ for the bus when it finally arrived.
explain: A longer past action that was interrupted uses was/were + -ing. Example: I was reading when you called.

notes.have waited: Have waited doesn't fit a finished past story.

q: I've lived here ___ three years.
explain: For + a length of time; since + a starting point. Example: for two weeks, since Monday.

notes.since: Since needs a starting point: since 2023.
notes.during: During means inside a period: during the summer.

q: You ___ wear a coat. It's warm today.
explain: Don't have to = it isn't necessary. Example: You don't have to come, but you can.

notes.mustn't: Mustn't means it is not allowed. Wearing a coat isn't wrong!
notes.have to: Have to means it IS necessary, but it's warm.
notes.must: Must also means it is necessary.

q: It's the ___ shop in the village.
explain: Good → better → best. Example: She is my best friend.

notes.goodest: Goodest isn't a word. Good is irregular.
notes.most good: Most good isn't used. Say best.

q: Did you ___ the new bakery?
explain: After did, use the plain verb. Example: Did you see it?

notes.visited: Did already shows the past, so no -ed.

q: If it rains, we ___ stay inside.
explain: First conditional: if + present, will + verb. Example: If you call, I will come.

notes.would: Would is for unreal situations: If I had wings, I would fly.
notes.are: Are can't go before 'stay' like this.

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: I have never seen a real dragon.
explain: Present perfect + never: I have never seen…

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: Could you pass me the sugar, please?
explain: Polite request: Could you + verb…, please?

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: There isn't any milk in the fridge.
explain: Negative with uncountable nouns: there isn't any…

q: Build the sentence in the candy shop!
answer: My brother is good at drawing.
explain: good at + -ing.

q: No more cake for me, thanks. I ___ already eaten three slices!
explain: Present perfect: have + past participle, often with already. Example: I have already finished.

notes.was: Was eaten would mean the slices ate you!

q: When I was young, I ___ climb trees every day.
explain: Used to + verb = a past habit that has stopped. Example: I used to have long hair.

notes.use to: After 'I' in the past it's used to, with a d.
notes.was used: Was used means someone used you.
notes.am used to: Am used to means 'I'm comfortable with' now.

q: Is there ___ bread left?
explain: In questions we usually use any. Example: Is there any milk?

notes.some: Some is mostly in positive sentences: There is some bread.
notes.many: Many is for countable plurals: many apples.
notes.a: A is for one countable thing. Bread is uncountable.

q: He runs ___ than his brother.
explain: Fast → faster. Example: A horse is faster than a dog.

notes.most fast: Most fast isn't used. Say fastest.

q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
explain: Going to = a prediction from what we can see now. Example: Look! He's going to fall!

notes.goes to: Goes to is a movement: He goes to school.

q: I ___ a shower when the phone rang.
explain: Past continuous for the longer action, past simple for the short one. Example: I was eating when he arrived.

notes.had: Had would mean the shower came after the call.
notes.have had: Have had is present perfect, not a story.

q: We ___ go to school on Saturdays. It's the weekend!
explain: Don't have to = not necessary. Example: I don't have to get up early on Sunday.

notes.mustn't: Mustn't means it's not allowed. Going isn't wrong!
notes.haven't: Haven't needs a past participle: haven't gone.

q: This is the girl ___ won the baking contest.
explain: Who is for people. Example: the boy who sings.

notes.which: Which is for things and animals.
notes.what: What isn't used to join a person to a sentence.

q: She's ___ excited to sleep!
explain: Too + adjective + to = more than is OK. Example: It's too hot to play.

notes.enough: Enough comes after the adjective: old enough.
notes.very much: Very much doesn't go before an adjective.
notes.so much: So much doesn't go before an adjective.

q: Have you finished your homework ___?
explain: Yet goes at the end of questions and negatives. Example: Has he arrived yet?

notes.already: Already usually goes in the middle of a positive sentence.
notes.still: Still is for something that hasn't stopped.
notes.ever: Ever asks 'at any time in your life'.

q: We ___ a sandcastle at the beach yesterday.
explain: Past simple for finished actions; build → built (irregular). Example: I built a den last week.

notes.build: Build is present; 'yesterday' needs the past.
notes.builded: Build is irregular: built, not builded.
notes.are building: Are building is happening now, not yesterday.

q: She ___ her lunch box at school on Monday.
explain: Forget → forgot (irregular past). Example: I forgot my hat.

notes.forgets: Forgets is present, for every day.

q: ___ you see the rainbow this morning?
explain: Past simple question: Did + subject + plain verb. Example: Did you eat breakfast?

notes.Were: Were goes with -ing or an adjective: Were you happy?
notes.Have: Have you seen…? doesn't fit 'this morning' with 'see'.

q: I didn't ___ the answer to question five.
explain: Didn't + plain verb. Example: He didn't come.

notes.knew: After didn't, use the plain verb, not the past.

q: The puppy ___ under the bed all afternoon.
explain: Sleep → slept. Example: I slept well.

q: We ___ at home last Sunday because it rained.
explain: Regular past: add -ed (stay → stayed).

q: Mia ___ a beautiful picture of a unicorn.
explain: Draw → drew → drawn. Past simple: drew. Example: He drew a map.

q: Where ___ you go on holiday last summer?
explain: Wh- question in the past: Where did you go?

q: At 8 p.m. yesterday I ___ my homework.
explain: Past continuous (was/were + -ing) for an action in progress at a past time.

notes.did: Did shows a finished action, not one in progress at 8 p.m.
notes.were doing: Were goes with you/we/they, not I.

q: While we ___ football, it started to snow.
explain: While + past continuous for the longer action. Example: While I was reading, the phone rang.

notes.played: Played is a finished action; 'while' needs the longer one in progress.
notes.was playing: Was is for I/he/she/it; we → were.

q: The children were sleeping when the owl ___.
explain: Long action (past continuous) + short action (past simple). Example: I was walking when I saw a fox.

notes.was hooting: The short action that interrupts uses the past simple.

q: I've ___ been to the seaside. I'd love to go!
explain: Present perfect + never = not at any time. Example: I've never flown a kite.

notes.ever: Ever is for questions: Have you ever…?
notes.yet: Yet goes at the end in questions or negatives.

q: Have you ___ seen a real penguin?
explain: Have you ever…? asks about experience in your life.

notes.never: Never is for statements: I've never…
notes.yet: Yet goes at the end of a sentence.
notes.since: Since needs a start time: since Monday.

q: We've ___ finished the puzzle! Look!
explain: Just = a very short time ago. Example: I've just eaten.

notes.yet: Yet goes at the end in questions and negatives.
notes.ever: Ever is for questions about experience.
notes.for: For needs a time: for two hours.

q: She has lived in Penang ___ she was five.
explain: Since + a start point; for + a length of time. Example: since Monday, for three days.

notes.for: For needs a length of time: for five years.
notes.ago: Ago goes with the past simple: five years ago.

q: They've had their hamster ___ two years.
explain: For + a length of time. Example: for ten minutes.

notes.since: Since needs a start point: since 2024.
notes.ago: Ago goes with the past simple.
notes.during: During needs a noun: during the holiday.

q: I haven't tidied my room ___.
explain: Not… yet = it hasn't happened, but it will. Example: I haven't eaten yet.

notes.already: Already is for things that have happened.
notes.ever: Ever is for questions about experience.

q: Tom ___ his arm, so he can't play today.
explain: Present perfect for a past action with a result now: has + past participle (broken).

notes.has broke: The participle is broken, not broke.
notes.is breaking: Is breaking means it's happening now.

q: Look at that wobbly tower! It's ___ fall!
explain: Going to for something we can see is about to happen.

notes.goes to: Goes to isn't a future form.

q: I'm cold. — I ___ close the window for you.
explain: Will ('ll) for a quick offer or decision made now.

notes.'m going: Going to is for plans made before.
notes.am: Am doesn't make an offer here.

q: We ___ visit Grandma next Saturday. It's planned.
explain: Going to for plans. Example: I'm going to learn the piano.

q: What ___ you do this weekend? — We're going camping!
explain: Present continuous for fixed plans: What are you doing this weekend?

q: I think it ___ be sunny tomorrow.
explain: I think + will for a prediction. Example: I think you'll win.

q: A cheetah is ___ than a tortoise.
explain: Short adjective + -er + than. Example: tall → taller than.

notes.fastest: Fastest is for the top of a group.
notes.fast: We need the -er form before than.

q: This is the ___ story in the whole book!
explain: the + adjective + -est for the top one; y → iest.

q: My new bike is ___ than my old one.
explain: Long adjectives: more + adjective + than.

notes.most comfortable: Most is for the top of a group.

q: Today is ___ than yesterday. I need a coat!
explain: cold → colder than.

q: This maze is ___ the one at school. Both are hard!
explain: as + adjective + as = the same.

notes.as hard than: As goes with as, not than.

q: Ben's drawing is good, but Ana's is ___.
explain: good → better → best (irregular).

notes.best: Best is for the top of a group.

q: That was the ___ day of my life!
explain: bad → worse → worst.

q: A whale is ___ animal in the sea.
explain: the + -est; double the last letter: big → biggest.

q: There isn't ___ juice left. Can we buy some?
explain: Much for things we can't count (juice, milk) in questions and negatives.

notes.many: Many is for countable things: many cups.
notes.a few: A few is for countable things.

q: How ___ sweets are in the jar?
explain: How many + plural countable noun.

notes.lot: Lot needs a: a lot of.

q: I have ___ friends in my new class. Only three!
explain: A few + plural countable noun = a small number.

notes.a little: A little is for uncountable things.
notes.a lot: A lot needs 'of', and three isn't a lot.

q: Can I have ___ milk in my tea, please? Just a bit.
explain: A little + uncountable = a small amount.

notes.a few: A few is for countable things.

q: Is there ___ cheese in the fridge?
explain: Any in questions and negatives. Example: Have you got any pets?

notes.some: Some is usually for positive sentences and offers.

q: Would you like ___ grapes?
explain: Some in offers: Would you like some cake?

notes.any: Any is for questions that aren't offers, and negatives.

q: You ___ run near the pool. It's dangerous!
explain: Mustn't = it's not allowed.

notes.don't have to: Don't have to = it's not necessary, but OK.
notes.can: Can means it's allowed, the opposite.

q: You ___ bring a pen. We have lots.
explain: Don't have to = it isn't necessary.

notes.can't: Can't means you aren't able or allowed.
notes.shouldn't: Shouldn't means it's a bad idea.

q: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
explain: Should + verb for advice.

notes.can't: Can't is the opposite of advice.

q: ___ I borrow your rubber, please?
explain: Could I…? is a polite request.

notes.Must: Must I…? asks if it's necessary.
notes.Will I: Will I…? asks about the future.

q: When I was four, I ___ read. Now I can!
explain: Couldn't = past of can't.

q: I ___ finish my project tonight. It's due tomorrow!
explain: I have to + verb = it's necessary.

q: I enjoy ___ in the rain.
explain: Enjoy + -ing. Example: She enjoys reading.

q: We want ___ the dinosaur museum.
explain: Want + to + verb.

notes.visit: We need to before the verb.

q: My brother is good at ___ jokes.
explain: Preposition (at) + -ing.

q: Let's stop ___ and start the game!
explain: Stop + -ing = finish doing something.

notes.to talk: Stop to talk means you stop in order to talk.

q: She decided ___ a cake for her mum.
explain: Decide + to + verb.

q: This is the dragon ___ lives in the cave.
explain: Which/that for animals and things.

q: That's the park ___ we had our picnic.
explain: Where for places.

notes.which: Which needs 'in': which we had our picnic in.

q: She's the teacher ___ helped me with maths.
explain: Who for people.

notes.which: Which is for things and animals.

q: I'm really good ___ swimming.
explain: good at + -ing / noun.

notes.in: We say good at, not good in.

q: Are you afraid ___ spiders?
explain: afraid of + noun.

q: We're going to the beach ___ bus.
explain: by + transport (no 'the'): by bus, by car.

notes.in: In needs 'the' or a car: in the car.

q: My birthday is ___ 5th May.
explain: On + a date. Example: on 1st June.

notes.in: In is for months alone: in May.

q: I'll see you ___ the weekend.
explain: British English: at the weekend.

notes.in: In the weekend isn't usual in British English.
notes.by the: By the weekend means 'before it ends'.

q: She plays ___ piano every day.
explain: Play + the + instrument: play the guitar.

notes.a: We use the, not a, with instruments.
notes.an: Piano starts with p, so not an.

q: We go to ___ school by bike.
explain: go to school (no article) when you go there to learn.

notes.the: Go to the school is for visiting the building.
notes.an: An is before a vowel sound.

q: The tortoise walked very ___.
explain: Adverb (how?) = adjective + -ly.

notes.slow: Slow is an adjective; we need slowly after walked.

q: She sings ___!
explain: beautiful → beautifully (adverb).

q: He did ___ in the spelling test. 20 out of 20!
explain: good (adjective) → well (adverb).

notes.good: Good describes a noun: a good test.

q: I ___ eat vegetables. I love broccoli!
explain: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb. Always = every time.

notes.never: Never means not at any time, but you love broccoli.

q: You like chocolate, ___ you?
explain: Positive sentence → negative tag: You like…, don't you?

notes.do: The tag must be negative here.

q: It isn't raining, ___ it?
explain: Negative sentence → positive tag.

notes.isn't: The tag must be positive here.
notes.does: Is raining uses be, not do.

q: ___ did you get to the party? — By car.
explain: How asks about the way.

q: ___ bag is this? — It's Lily's.
explain: Whose asks who owns something.

q: ___ do you go to the dentist? — Twice a year.
explain: How often asks about frequency.

notes.How much: How much asks about amount or price.
notes.How long: How long asks about time length.

q: These aren't my crayons. They're ___.
explain: Possessive pronouns stand alone: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.

q: The twins love ___ new kitten.
explain: Their + noun = belonging to them.

q: Did you make this card ___?
explain: Reflexive pronoun: you → yourself.

notes.you: You doesn't give the meaning 'on your own'.

q: The dog wagged ___ tail.
explain: Its = belonging to it (no apostrophe).

q: If you heat ice, it ___.
explain: Zero conditional for facts: If + present, present.

q: If we finish early, we ___ play a game.
explain: First conditional: If + present, will + verb.

q: I wanted to go out, ___ it was raining.
explain: But shows a contrast.

notes.because: Because gives a reason, not a contrast.

q: We took umbrellas ___ it was raining.
explain: Because gives the reason.

notes.so: So gives a result, not a reason.

q: It was late, ___ we went home.
explain: So gives the result.

q: I'll wait here ___ you come back.
explain: Until = up to the time when.

notes.since: Since needs a past start point.
notes.for: For needs a length of time.

q: Brush your teeth ___ you go to bed.
explain: Before = earlier than.

notes.after: After would mean brushing in bed!
notes.while: While means at the same time.
notes.since: Since needs a past start point.

q: My cousin ___ in Japan since last summer.
explain: Present perfect + since for something that started in the past and is still true. Example: I've been at this school since 2024.

notes.was: Was would mean it's finished, but since shows it's still true.
notes.goes: Goes doesn't go with in Japan since.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Yesterday = past: go → went.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: He/she/it: doesn't. She doesn't like spiders.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Comparing two people: short adjectives add -er + than: taller than.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Many for things you can count: many books.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: We/you/they + were.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: going to + verb (no -ing): going to visit.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Last weekend we ___ a film and ___ popcorn.
explain: Last weekend = past: watched, ate.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Is ___ any milk? There isn't ___ juice.
explain: Is there any…? / There isn't any…

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: She's ___ than her brother but not as ___ as her dad.
explain: taller than; as tall as.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
explain: We do homework; after dinner.
